channel.title: Global Arbitration Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Arbitration Review (globalarbitrationreview.com)

item.title: New practice head at Houthoff
item.description: Thomas Stouten has been appointed the new head of international arbitration at Houthoff, taking over from Dirk Knottenbelt.

item.title: Mourre shares his take on abuse of process
item.description: In a speech at King's College London before the New Year, Alexis Mourre considered abuse of process in international arbitration with reference to "diametrically opposed conclusions" on the matter from Emmanuel Gaillard and Jan Paulsson.

item.title: Libya revives challenge to Turkish contractor’s award
item.description: The French courts have enforced a final award in a treaty claim against Libya relating to three construction projects, while reviving the state’s challenge to a jurisdictional award in the same case.

item.title: US gymnast wins challenge to CAS award as Gharavi cleared of conflict
item.description: A Swiss court has granted a request by US gymnast Jordan Chiles to reopen a high-profile Court of Arbitration for Sport award that effectively stripped her of an Olympic bronze medal – while dismissing her claims that the presiding arbitrator Hamid Gharavi had a conflict of interests.

item.title: Potential liability of witnesses and experts providing false testimony in international arbitration
item.description: Potential liability of witnesses and experts providing false testimony in international arbitration

item.title: CAS announces line-up for Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport will open two temporary offices for the upcoming Olympic Winter Games in Milan and the alpine town of Cortina d'Ampezzo, north Italy, to settle sports-related and anti-doping disputes in a quick timeframe.

item.title: Chinese firm hires from A&O Shearman and HSF Kramer
item.description: Hui Zhong Law Firm has added to its international arbitration team in Hong Kong, hiring Kitty Zheng as a partner from A&O Shearman and Wu Hao as of counsel from Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer.

item.title: IBA panel explores “the electrification of everything”
item.description: A panel at the International Bar Association Arbitration Day in Abu Dhabi explored how the surge in demand for electricity is impacting the energy market and the types of disputes arising in the sector.

item.title: Telecom Italia fails to halt revival of US$15 billion claim
item.description: The French Court of Cassation has upheld the annulment of an ICC award that dismissed a Brazilian private equity group’s US$15 billion claim against Telecom Italia.

item.title: Bulgaria sees off Czech utility’s billion-euro ECT claim
item.description: Czech utility ČEZ has lost a billion-euro Energy Charter Treaty claim against Bulgaria over changes to the country’s electricity market – as the European Commission formally calls on 16 EU member states to withdraw from the treaty.
